newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BUSHFIRE DANGER EASES AFTER RAIN
The bushfire danger in New South Wales and Queensland has eased after overnight rain.
Fires in the Severn region near Glen Innes in the north of New South Wales were brought under control by firefighters yesterday, but continued to burn.
Bush Fire Services says an aerial survey later today will see if the rain has put out the flames.
Meanwhile, rain across south-east Queensland and the southern Downs overnight and this morning appear to have helped fire-fighters working to contain several blazes.
FIRST EUTHANASIA DEATH STILL BEING PROBED
Terminally ill people wanting to die under the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law face a new obstacle, with news that the first death under the legislation is still being investigated.
The death certificate for Bob Dent, who asked for a lethal injection over two months ago, reveals that his cause of death is still "subject to investigation".
A Territory Government source says the possibility of a coronial inquest places a major obstacle in front of any patient seeking to use the euthanasia law.
Meantime, Darwin Doctor Philip Nitschke, says a change of mind by Mr Dent's son, could encourage politicians to heed community support for the law.
Rod Dent has called for best practice in palliative care, instead of euthanasia, but Dr Nitschke says Rod Dent was directed by the Liberal Party of which he's a member.
ROADSIDE TESTS FOR VICTORIAN DRIVERS PROPOSED
People suspected of driving under the influence of drugs in Victoria will have to carry out roadside tests if a recommendation from a Parliamentary Committee is taken up.
The committee wants to see a new offence of driving while impaired introduced.
It recommends motorists suspected of using drugs like cannabis or amphetamines be made to do roadside tests.

Chairman of the committee, John Richardson, says the first roadside tests would be simple things like walking the straight line and touching your nose... similar to tests carried out in New South Wales and Los Angeles. - - - -
VOLCANIC ISLAND COULD BE WORLD HERITAGE LISTED
The home of Australia's only active volcano is being considered for World Heritage listing in Mexico this week.
Heard Island, halfway between South Africa and Australia, is one of three sub-Antarctic islands being discussed by a UNESCO committee.
The island was formed around a volcanic mountain mass named Big Ben and is still active.
The other two islands, McDonald and Macquarie are also being assessed for their world heritage potential.
Although all three islands have a history of sealing only Macquarie Island is used regularly for research and tourism.
